beforeSession: Choose four to six paper signal cards for the table; place blank paper and pencils within reach.
Say that every porch-light mark is pretend and belongs to a made-up story setting.
Pick one writing goal: start, problem, helper, mood, or ending.
Give each writer a choice of two cards, then let the adult read the prompt aloud.
Keep the first draft short: one sentence, three sentences, or a tiny scene.
paperSignalSetup: Print cards on plain paper or cardstock and cut along the card edges.
Sort cards into color, pattern, message, mood, object, and ending piles.
Set a pencil cup, blank slips, and a scrap-paper spot in the center.
Use a paper clip or folder to keep unused cards together between sessions.
Mark a sample card as the adult example, then invite writers to make their own signal marks.
storySignalCoaching: Ask what the signal tells the character to notice next.
Turn one-word answers into story sentences by adding who, where, and why.
When a writer gets stuck, offer two gentle choices instead of supplying the whole idea.
Point to the card color or shape before asking for more detail.
Let funny, odd, or quiet ideas stay; the goal is a usable story seed.
privacyAndSafetyNotes: Use invented labels, role words, or blank spaces for every person on the story signal cards.
Use broad place words instead of private details or named locations.
Keep every story signal card offline with the family adult, tutor, or table host.
Sharing stays optional and limited to one invented word, sketch, or line.
Check every take-home slip for private details before it leaves the adult-led table.
familyHandoff: Send only the paper slip and a short note about the story skill practiced.
Tell family adults the signals are fiction cues for paper stories.
Invite a writer to read one favorite sentence aloud during a calm table moment.
Suggest that families add one extra line, one title, or one ending choice.
Return slips in a folder or envelope for the next adult-led session.
reset: Collect used cards and blank slips.
Recycle torn scraps and save clear drafts in the folder.
Shuffle each card pile so the next group sees a fresh mix.
Note which cue type helped most, then start the next session with that type.

signalRoutines.name: Color Glow Quickwrite
steps: Adult fans three color cue cards face up.
Writer chooses one color and says what feeling it gives the scene.
Everyone writes one sentence that uses the color signal.
Adult invites one volunteer sentence, then moves to a new card.

signalRoutines.name: Pattern Pass
steps: Adult gives one pattern card to the first writer.
Writer adds a sentence with a repeated mark or shape.
Pass the card to the next writer at the table.
Adult ends after each writer has added one line.

signalRoutines.name: Message Flip
signalRoutines.bestFor: Reluctant writers who need a clear next move.
steps: Adult folds a blank slip and places it under a message cue card.
Writer writes a short fictional signal message on the slip.
Adult flips a question cue card beside it.
Writer answers as the character and turns the answer into a scene line.

signalRoutines.name: Mood Dimmer
signalRoutines.bestFor: Revising a sentence so it carries a stronger feeling.
steps: Adult chooses one plain sentence from a draft.
Writer places a mood cue above the sentence.
Writer rewrites the sentence to match that mood.
Adult circles one stronger verb or describing word.

signalRoutines.name: Object Signal Swap
signalRoutines.bestFor: Adding concrete details to a short scene.
steps: Adult places an object cue beside a porch-light card.
Writer names what the character carries or finds.
Writer writes one reason the object matters.
Swap the object cue and revise one noun or action.

signalRoutines.name: Ending Glow
signalRoutines.bestFor: Finishing short drafts that stop too soon.
steps: Adult chooses an ending cue and reads it aloud.
Writer picks a quiet, funny, or surprising ending path.
Writer writes the last two lines on paper.
Adult asks what changed from the first line to the last.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Color Glow Sentence
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Pick one pretend porch-light color and write what it means: ____________________.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family adds one describing word in the blank: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Band Pattern Clue
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Draw a paper pattern beside the signal, then write what it tells the character: ____________________.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family says one extra pattern idea to add here: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Tiny Message Card
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Write a three-word message from the pretend signal: ____________________.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family chooses one word to make clearer: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Mood Glow Shift
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Write one line twice: first calm, then silly. Silly version: ____________________.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family names the mood they heard: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Object Beside the Signal
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Invent one object near the paper signal and explain why it matters: ____________________.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family adds one detail about the object: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: First Next Last
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Use three short beats: first the signal appears, next ____________________, last the character decides.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family fills the middle beat with a gentle twist: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Sound-Like Signal
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Make up a quiet sound for the pretend signal and write it here: ____________________.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family repeats the sound softly and adds one action: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Helper Glow
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Invent a helper who understands the signal and write the helper's first idea: ____________________.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family adds the helper's kind phrase: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Setting Circle
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Name a made-up setting for the card, then write one detail: ____________________.
takeHomeSignalSlips.familyLine: Family adds one color, shape, or texture: ____________________.

takeHomeSignalSlips.title: Question Glow
takeHomeSignalSlips.direction: Ask the signal one story question and leave the answer for the character: ____________________.

optionalSharePrompts: I want to read the sentence where the signal changes the character plan: ____________________.
My favorite made-up signal color is ____________________ because it makes the scene feel clear.
One pattern I used more than once was ____________________.
The kindest helper line in my story was ____________________.
The funniest object near the pretend porch-light card was ____________________.
A question my character still has is ____________________.
The ending I chose can be summed up in five words: ____________________.
One detail I revised to make clearer is ____________________.
